html:
The bunkers of Albania are about 170,000 small concrete pillboxes built between 1967 and 1986 on the orders of Enver Hoxha, who feared invasion by Yugoslavia, NATO or the Warsaw Pact.

After the Soviet invasion of Czechoslovakia in 1968, Hoxha wanted every citizen ready to fight. Mushroom shaped domes appeared on beaches, mountain passes, farms and city parks, about one for every few square kilometres. Building them took a huge share of the country's cement and money in a time of shortages. They were never used. After communism fell, many were broken up for their steel, while others became cafes, shelters for animals or museums, such as the Bunk'Art centres in Tirana. They are the best known relic of communist Albania.
